items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: Jolly Row Martin, I know him well. I used to play with him too.

ctx.x: Oh, did you ever run into Jolly Row Martin, the Wyandand boy?

Jolly Row Martin, I know him well. I used to play with him too. Where? He was from Monroe, Monroe, Louisiana. He was around Shreeport. When we had the band there, he used to come around and sit around, you know, and play something. He'd be working on a job like that. He'd tell the fellas, get up, let me play something. He'd get up and he'd play something, you know. That's the way the musicians were.
Did he play pool a lot in those days, do you remember? Huh? Did Jolly Row play pool much in those days too? Pool?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: Jelly Roll? Uh-huh. I don't know him this piano school.

ctx.x: Well, he worked with different fellows. He worked on Bourbon Street sometimes, and different places, spots around. During the time I was working on Ivoryville Street for the E-light, because I used to meet him, going to wake, and sometimes we'd go over together on the boat in the morning. He used to wake all around in Vichy Corral.
What about Jelly Roll Morton? You said you knew him too, huh?

Jelly Roll? Uh-huh. I don't know him this piano school. He used to be here a while back on Bayeson Street. And he left here. He went around Monroe, went home, and from there he'd come back here again. He played piano all over around Vichy Corral, mostly on Basin Street, mostly. Who would he be working for? And in 1917, he went back home again in 1917, he came to Chicago. And he'd be around at 35th and State at the E-light Cabaret. Used to visit there, you know.
